chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O brother of Jau'f! Indeed, faith (Iman) is superior to submission (Islam), and indeed conviction (Yaqeen) is superior to faith, and there is nothing more precious than conviction.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Islam, Iman, and Yaqeen in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates a spiritual hierarchy where Islam represents outward submission, Iman signifies internalized faith, and Yaqeen denotes the highest state of unwavering certainty. This distinction reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the depth of conviction (yaqeen) as the ultimate perfection of belief, transcending mere ritualistic adherence. The Prophet’s address to Jabir as 'Akhā Jua'f' highlights the intimate, familial nature of this transmission within the Ahl al-Bayt tradition.
